Subject: Quick follow-up on PHI handling & hosting options

Thanks again for the demo earlier — helpful conversation. A couple of follow-ups from our side so procurement can start evaluation: 

1) BAA: does Redwood provide a standard BAA? If so, can you confirm whether the BAA covers the hosted (multi-tenant) API, or is it limited to dedicated/private deployments?

2) PHI handling boundaries: we need a clear matrix indicating which deployment modes allow persistent PHI storage, what data is cached (KV/embedding/LLM cache) and what our responsibilities vs Redwood's are for encryption, logging, and deletion.

3) Eligible hosting modes: for our architecture we need to know whether the following are available and supported for PHI workloads: Redwood Hosted with contractual BAA, Redwood Dedicated (single-tenant pool), Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). Please call out any limitations (e.g., region locks, egress restrictions, required network peering).

4) Evidence: procurement expects SOC 2 type II report availability and a timeline for evidence call (if any).

Can you share a short hosting-matrix and an initial BAA (even a redline-friendly draft) so we can loop in legal and security? Procurement contact copied on this thread.

Attachment: recording attached.

Best,

Hi Anika — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the recording. Quick answers and proposed next steps below.

Short answers (high level):
- BAA: Redwood signs BAAs. We can sign for Hosted, but the hosted path for PHI requires specific controls (dedicated tenancy and contractual language) — many customers prefer Dedicated or Private for full isolation.
- PHI boundaries: we will produce a one-page hosting matrix that indicates where PHI may be persisted (embeddings store, KV cache, logs) and the shared-responsibility split (what we manage vs what you configure).
- Eligible modes: Hosted w/BAA (with dedicated tenancy option) — supported; Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) — supported and recommended for higher isolation; Private (VPC/on-prem) — supported and best for regulated deployments. Region residency and egress constraints are configurable; we'll call those out per region.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II is available under NDA; we can schedule an evidence call the week of Oct 19.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I will send the hosting matrix and a redline-friendly BAA draft by EOD Oct 14. (Attached: draft matrix stub + placeholder BAA).
2) Schedule a 30-min SOC 2 evidence call for Oct 19 — please confirm preferred time.
3) Procurement: please send the SOW template or any specific commercial redlines you expect; we'll have our contracts team ready.

Notes on technical nuance:
- Cache behavior: LLM KV cache is ephemeral by default but embeddings and persistent stores are configurable; if you need zero-persistence we can enable prefix caching only and manage ephemeral sessions.
- Tokenization/PII handling: we can provide guidance on in-flight redaction and recommend client-side tokenization for highest control.

Attachments: redwood-phi-hosting-matrix.xlsx (matrix with columns for deployment, persistence, encryption, access controls), redwood-baa-draft.pdf (initial BAA)

Let me know if you want a quick walkthrough of the matrix with Aditya and me.

Best,

Paige / Anika — looping in timeline and concrete deliverables so procurement/legal have what they need.

Deliverables and timeline (working target):
- Oct 14 (EOD PT): PDF & spreadsheet hosting matrix (deployment modes, persistence columns, encryption/KMS options, shared-responsibility checklist) + redline-friendly BAA draft.
- Oct 15: short tech appendix describing cache behaviors (KV, embeddings, session cache) and options to disable persistent embeddings for PHI traffic.
- Oct 19: SOC 2 evidence call (30min). Proposed times: 9:00am or 10:30am PT — please confirm which works.
- After SOC 2 call: provide SOC 2 cover letter and pointer to secure evidence package under NDA within 48 hours.

Short answers to the specific procurement asks you flagged: 
- KV cache vs embeddings: KV cache is ephemeral and scoped to active sessions (can be configured to be non-persistent). Embeddings are stored in a managed vector store by default; we can configure a PHI policy to prevent persistence or route embeddings to a customer-controlled store in Dedicated/Private.
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256 at rest. Customer-managed keys (KMS) are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; Hosted with BAA supports KMS with contractual commitments (region-dependent).
- Residency: US-only residency supported via region pinning in Dedicated and Private. Hosted (shared) paths may require explicit tenancy selection and region pinning — we'll flag any feature limitations in the matrix.

Next steps for procurement/legal: Paige, I uploaded the draft BAA and hosting matrix to a shared Drive folder (link below). We'll prepare a short walkthrough on Oct 14 afternoon if you prefer.
